analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations (Sean Vogel, 29 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Hyperscaler earnings were messy on headlines but the compute trajectory is robust. One mega cap platform fell about 10% after hours on consumer ad misses while Cloud growth stayed strong. The other beat cloud whispers with positive quarterly FCF and expanding contracted obligations.

The light capex print reflected third-party facility delivery sequencing, not lower appetite, and next quarter's capex is guided back up. Power and cluster delivery remain the main bottlenecks. The desk says the market has moved past questioning capex durability and now asks about value capture and returns on capital.

Oracle rallied double digits after management laid out a path to positive FCF in H2 FY28 and $30bn+ in FY29, with capex stepping down in FY29. Incremental capital raises are capped at $20bn through FY30, excluding refinancing. The desk calls it potentially very significant for levered AI credit but wants to see spreads respond.

Oracle guided to non-GAAP operating margins of 40%+ by FY30 on $225bn+ revenue, with high-20s project returns and about $16bn annualized revenue per fully ramped gigawatt. The desk notes this depends on execution, utilization and financing assumptions.

Fed held at 3.75-4.00% with two hawkish dissents (Cook, Hammack, both preferring a 25bp hike). The statement upgraded activity to 'strong' from 'solid' and kept inflation 'elevated'. Richard Privorotsky reads Warsh as balanced, still sees December as a hike, and expects little repricing. He calls it a volatility-suppressing event.

ECB meets with two hikes since June already done. French sovereign stress is tightening conditions, and European gas near €100/MWh makes a dovish pivot unlikely. The desk sees some room for repricing if financial conditions get more airtime.

Energy and geopolitics: the desk reads Vance's letter to Iran as a last-minute bid for a diplomatic win, with no sign of Iranian capitulation, and thinks the path leads toward post-midterm escalation. European equities are looking through €100 gas and elevated oil. A pre-midterm US/Iran meeting is the 'geopolitical lottery ticket'.

Risk view: the pain trade is hyperscalers underperforming while de-risked picks-and-shovels names work. The market is moving from rewarding capex growth to demanding evidence of returns. Micro stays supportive and the desk expects dips to be bought, with credit the most important thing to watch.

Asia: Samsung disappointed, especially on shareholder returns versus a higher bar after Hynix. Advantest surged on a significant guidance upgrade, which the desk takes as a reminder of robust AI demand.

US close: S&P +28bps at 7,744 with a $1.3bn MOC to sell. NDX +55bps at 29,813, R2K +15bps at 2,823, Dow +19bps at 52,476. VIX -565bps at 16.53, WTI +139bps at $101.27, US 10Y unchanged at 5.0217%, gold +50bps at 4,072, DXY -16bps at 102.16, Bitcoin +115bps at $81,584. Volume was 16.606bn shares against a YTD daily average of 18.494bn.

Equities were supported by cleared capital-raise overhangs (META, SPCX), better tech prints overnight (SKHY, VRT), Oracle's reaffirmed guide at its investor day, and a Fed non-event. After hours, MSFT rose about 4% on a beat (revenue +19% y/y, Azure +48% versus +43% last quarter, not comparable due to re-segmentation) while GOOGL fell about 7% as Search growth of +12% missed the +14% expectation, which may feed a share-loss narrative.

Flow: demand returned in AI/Semis after 2-3 weeks of little buying, mostly from long-only accounts. Asset managers and hedge funds were small net buyers, and the desk rated floor activity 4 out of 10.

Derivatives: S&P and NDX vols were offered across the curve and skew eased slightly. Call volumes are above the YTD average and short-dated tech upside buying is picking up in outright and call spread form. GS clients bought ORCL call spreads in 6Nov and 27Nov. The desk prefers NDX over S&P, with call spreads the preferred upside structure. Long dealer gamma is concentrated to the topside, pinning the S&P to its range. Implied move into the election is a 1.24% straddle to next Tuesday's close.

earnings_insights: MSFT after-hours (reported 10/29): total revenue +19% y/y versus +17% y/y cc last quarter, Azure +48% versus +43% last quarter, not apples to apples due to re-segmentation. Stock up about 4% after hours.
GOOGL after-hours (reported 10/29): Search growth +12% versus expectations of +14%, Cloud growth solid. Stock down about 7% after hours.

Oracle investor day (10/29): path to positive FCF in H2 FY28 and $30bn+ in FY29, capex stepping down in FY29, incremental capital raises capped at $20bn through FY30 excluding refinancing, non-GAAP operating margin 40%+ by FY30 on $225bn+ revenue. These are management targets, not reported results.

A second hyperscaler (unnamed in the report) beat cloud whispers with positive quarterly FCF and expanding total contracted obligations. Its capex looked light because of third-party facility delivery timing, and next quarter is guided higher.
One unnamed mega cap platform fell about 10% after hours on consumer ad misses while Cloud growth remained robust.
Advantest raised guidance significantly. Samsung disappointed on shareholder returns. Hynix, SKHY and VRT printed better-than-expected results overnight.

tension_points.bull_case: Underlying compute trajectory and AI demand remain robust. Aggregate spending intentions are flat to higher and Advantest's upgrade reinforces demand. The desk expects dips to be bought.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is moving from rewarding capex growth to demanding evidence of returns. Hyperscalers could weigh on sentiment, and the pain trade is hyperscalers underperforming.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Levered AI credit spreads failing to respond to Oracle's funding outline, which the desk calls the most important thing to watch.

tension_points.bull_case: French sovereign stress is doing some tightening for the ECB, leaving room for repricing if financial conditions get more airtime.
tension_points.bear_case: With European gas at €100/MWh and second-round inflation effects, a dovish pivot is unlikely and another hike in December is possible.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lagarde giving more weight to financial conditions and sovereign pressure than to underlying inflation and energy second-round effects.
